seo_title: Cost of Living in Izmir 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Izmir per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: Turkey's third-largest city on the Aegean Sea: visa-free entry for 90 days, a mild climate and a calmer pace than Istanbul. Great for remote work by the sea, though some districts are closed to residence permits.
pros: Visa-free entry for 90 days within six months
A mild Mediterranean climate and a six-month swimming season
Calmer and cheaper than Istanbul, yet still a big seaside city
A secular, European-spirited city with the Kordon waterfront
Fresh seafood, markets and a strong coffee culture
cons: Some districts are closed to the tourist residence permit — getting an ikamet is harder
High lira inflation: prices and rents are rising fast
A smaller Russian-speaking community than in Antalya or Alanya
Hot and crowded in summer — tough without air conditioning

visa_steps.title: Visa-free entry
visa_steps.description: Up to 90 days within 180 — on a passport, with a stamp at the border.

visa_steps.title: Rental with a contract
visa_steps.description: An ikamet requires a notarised rental contract; check in advance whether the district is open.

visa_steps.title: Tax number
visa_steps.description: A vergi numarası is issued free at the tax office — needed for a bank and bills.

visa_steps.title: Bank account
visa_steps.description: Enpara, Ziraat or DenizBank — opening is possible with a passport and tax number.

visa_steps.title: Ikamet (residence permit)
visa_steps.description: A short-term one-year permit via rental, study or business; in some Izmir districts issuance is restricted.

faq.question: Do Russian citizens need a visa for Izmir?
faq.answer: No, up to 90 days visa-free. For living there people get an ikamet (residence permit), but in some Izmir districts issuance via rental is restricted.

faq.question: Which language is spoken in Izmir?
faq.answer: Turkish; English is known in tourist spots and among young people, with little Russian in everyday life.

faq.question: Can I pay with a Russian card in Izmir?
faq.answer: MIR cards and Russian Visa/Mastercard don't work. People open a local card with a Turkish bank.

faq.question: What is the climate like in Izmir?
faq.answer: Mediterranean: hot dry summers and mild rainy winters. You can swim from May to October.

faq.question: How does Izmir differ from Istanbul?
faq.answer: Calmer, cheaper and right by the sea, without Istanbul's traffic or scale — but with less work and community.

faq.question: How is work in Izmir?
faq.answer: Mostly remote; the local market requires Turkish. Freelancing and online business are popular.

reviews.text: We moved from Istanbul for the sea and the calm. Alsancak is top for living, but we did the ikamet through an agent: the open-district rules are a hassle.
A dream climate and affordable seafood. The downside is the volatile lira — they raised our rent almost twofold in a year.
